problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{21}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}]$ if its determinant is $71.$
worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{21}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{12}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{12} & =(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-3-10) \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{21}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{12}=\frac{1}{71}\cdot 13=\frac{13}{71}.\end{aligned}
$$
